items.question: What does reading a stored value that matches no status return?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.chose: Returns null for any value that is not a status or a known old spelling, and never maps it to the nearest status.
items.instead: Throw an error, or fall back to a default status such as draft.

items.question: How loosely are stored values matched to a status when read (case, surrounding whitespace, separators)?
items.chose: Trims the ends, lowercases, and turns each run of whitespace, '-' or '_' into one space. It then matches exactly, so 'Merged-' and '_Review_' read as statuses.
items.instead: Only trim and lowercase, so '-' and '_' are not treated as separators. Or match case-sensitively.

items.question: Which old free-text spellings are read as a status, and what do they map to?
items.ticket: Sandbox status is stored as free text (draft, Draft, in-review...)
items.chose: Maps only the cleaned form 'in review' (so 'in-review', 'In  Review' and similar) to review. No other aliases are mapped.
items.instead: Map more aliases, such as 'in_progress', 'done' or 'open'. Or map nothing and rely on cleaning alone.

items.question: Does a separator in the middle of a status word (e.g. 'cla_imed', 're\tview') still read as that status?
items.chose: No. The separator becomes a space, so the cleaned value no longer matches and the read returns null.
items.instead: Remove separators entirely, so 'cla_imed' reads as claimed.

items.question: What does reading an empty or whitespace-only value return?
items.chose: Returns null, because the cleaned empty string matches nothing.
items.instead: Treat it as draft, the default state, or throw.

items.question: Does writing accept non-canonical input, such as 'Draft' or the old spelling 'in-review', by normalising it first?
items.chose: No. Only the exact lowercase enum strings pass. Anything else, including case variants and old spellings, is rejected.
items.instead: Normalise through readStatus before writing, so 'Draft' is written as 'draft' and 'in-review' as 'review'.

items.question: How does writing signal an invalid status?
items.chose: Throws a plain Error with the message 'not a sandbox status: "<value as given>"'.
items.instead: Return null or a result object, or throw a custom or typed error.

items.question: Does writing trim whitespace from the value before checking it?
items.chose: No. The value is checked as given, so ' draft' is rejected.
items.instead: Trim the value before validating it.

items.question: When reading many rows, what happens to a row whose status cannot be read?
items.chose: Keeps the row with its id and sets its status to null, and does not drop the row or throw.
items.instead: Drop the row from the output, or throw on the first unreadable row.

items.question: How are unreadable values reported when reading many rows (duplicates, form, order)?
items.chose: Lists the distinct raw stored values, such as 'Ghost ' with its trailing space, sorted with the default string sort.
items.instead: List ids of the unreadable rows, or list every occurrence in input order, or list the cleaned values.

items.question: Where is the enum applied to written values, given the ticket says to use it 'where the status is set'?
items.ticket: use it where the status is set
items.chose: Only adds writeStatus as a validator function. It changes no existing call sites that set a status, and none appear in the diff.
items.instead: Change the code that sets the status to call the validator or take the enum type.
